newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilgener holders agree capital increase.
newsitem.headline: Chilgener holders agree capital increase.

text.p: Shareholders in Chilean power electricity Chilgener on Tuesday approved a $500 million capital increase to finance new projects in Chile and the rest of Latin America.
The capital increase will take the form of share issue, but details were not immediately available.
The company's main projects include two power plants in Brazil, a power transmission line between Argentina and northern Chile and electricity privatizations in Peru.
Chilgener is also planning to bid in upcoming privatizations in Colombia, said officials.

The firm, Chile's second largest power generator, plans to invest around $1 billion in Latin America over the next five years, general manager Juan Antonio Guzman told reporters after the news conference.
Guzman said Chilgener was studying a range of projects worth $3.3 billion with foreign and local partners.
"These are all projects which the company has in various degrees of study. Chilgener's share should be around half of this," said Guzman.
These projects will be financed from Tuesday's capital increase with the rest likely to be debt, he said.
